translation.english_text: (Location: Kaliamman temple.)

source_locator.description: At the Parasakthi temple, Gunasekaran attacks the priest.

translation.english_text: (At the Parasakthi temple, Gunasekaran attacks the priest.)

source_locator.description: Festival activity, kavadi offerings and the man on the bier rising after the priest's intense puja.

notes: `பாடைக் காவடி` is retained as `paadai kavadi` rather than expanded through outside ritual knowledge.
translation.english_text: The priest's bustle, kavadi offerings, worship and archana to Ambal—the goddess festival is in full swing. A `paadai kavadi` comes to Parasakthi's sanctum. After the priest's intensely fervent puja, the man who had been on the bier gets up.
Mother! Parasakthi! I have paid the offering I owed for my son. Save my child, Mother.

notes: The invocation `ரீங்கரீம்` is retained phonetically rather than normalized.
translation.english_text: Om... Reengarim. What is wrong with your child's body, amma?

notes: This immutable record crosses PDF 49→50 and remains one unit.
The source clause around Ambal `குடிகொண்டிருந்தா` and the vow is syntactically pressure-sensitive; the English preserves the vow/result sequence without repairing the Tamil.
translation.english_text: If Ambal had taken residence and no affliction came to my son's body, I vowed to take a `paadai kavadi`. By her grace, he survived after losing only one eye. I have paid the offering too.

english_page_segments.english_text: If Ambal had taken residence and no affliction came to my son's body, I vowed to take a `paadai kavadi`.
By her grace, he survived after losing only one eye. I have paid the offering too.

translation.english_text: Don't be afraid. Your son will live a long life.

source_locator.description: A voice comes from behind the image of Parasakthi.

translation.english_text: (A voice comes from behind the image of Parasakthi.)
Hey, priest! First calculate your own horoscope.
Who? Is Ambal speaking?
When has Ambal ever spoken, you witless fellow?
Mother Parasakthi!

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran emerges from behind Ambal's image with loud laughter.

translation.english_text: (With loud laughter, Gunasekaran emerges from behind Ambal's image.)
Is this Parasakthi your mother? Is my sister Kalyani your slave, shameless man? Isn't that it?
Who are you, man? What is this calamity?

It is because you did not know calamity would come that you played with my sister. Great sinner who gives blessings to devotees, now you stand in the dock. Let all these people be judges; let them pronounce judgment.
Parasakthi! Parasakthi!

It will not speak. If stone could speak, when you dared to plunder my sister's chastity would it not have stopped you, saying, 'Hey priest, witless wretch, stop'? My sister, caught in your violent embrace, is said to have called that Parasakthi a thousand times. Did she run over and give her protection?
O masses of devotees! You're just standing there watching!

notes: `சுக்குமாந்தடி` is retained as `sukkumān thadi` because the verified source does not define the object more precisely.
translation.english_text: Why do you seek human help? Devotee of the goddess, when your goddess holds a trident, a whirling sword and a `sukkumān thadi`, why are you dying of fear?
Sacrilege! Sacrilege!

notes: This immutable dialogue crosses PDF 50→51 and remains one unit.
`ஆஸ்திகம் விதியாக்கிக் கொண்டது` is pressure-sensitive; the English keeps the source's theism/rule movement rather than replacing it with an external ideological label.
translation.english_text: Sacrilege. Is turning Ambal's sanctum into a men's room not sacrilege? Is making theism into a rule not sacrilege? Is turning it into a fortress of lust that seizes maidens' chastity not sacrilege? Hey priest, I have dared death. I know what reward there is for the deed I am about to do: the gallows, the gallows. Never mind. In this rotten society, let my act be a lesson to the crowd that keeps watching the drama in which fake priests like you put on the guise of holy men.

I know what reward there is for the deed I am about to do: the gallows, the gallows. Never mind. In this rotten society, let my act be a lesson to the crowd that keeps watching the drama in which fake priests like you put on the guise of holy men.

notes: The priest raising the sickle is embedded in the immutable dialogue record.
translation.english_text: What, man! You come making a commotion when we're celebrating a festival for the goddess! (The priest raises the sickle.)

notes: The disarming and final blow are embedded in the immutable dialogue record.
translation.english_text: (Snatching the sickle from the priest's hand.) Festival! A festival for you and your goddess, who thought to destroy my sister's life! No—here, a festival for this blade! A blood festival! A festival of valour! A victory festival! (He strikes the priest on the head.)
